paragraphs: Electricity in Ireland is the most expensive in the EU. A normal home pays more than €1,700 a year.
A new report says some easy changes could make bills lower. Wind Energy Ireland, a group for the wind power industry, published it on Monday.
The Government helps new wind farms with a support scheme. The report wants longer contracts, 20 years instead of 15. It also wants payments to go up when prices go up.
These changes could make power from new wind farms about 11 per cent cheaper. Some changes could start next year. More wind farms are being built now than at any time in ten years.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭的電費是歐盟最貴的。
一般家庭一年要付超過1,700歐元。
一份新報告說，一些簡單的改變可以讓電費降低。
代表風力發電業的團體「愛爾蘭風能協會」在週一發表了這份報告。
政府用一項補助方案來幫助新的風力發電場。
報告希望合約更長，從15年改成20年。
它也希望物價上漲時，補助金額跟著提高。
這些改變可以讓新風場的電力便宜大約11%。
有些改變明年就可以開始。
現在興建中的風場比過去十年任何時候都多。

paragraphs: Irish people pay the highest electricity prices in the European Union. A typical household now pays more than €1,700 a year, about 50 per cent more than the EU average.

A new report says some simple changes to a green energy scheme could help to bring bills down. The report was written by the consultants Baringa for Wind Energy Ireland, a group that represents the wind industry. It was published on Monday.

The Government supports new wind farms through the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme, or RESS. Companies compete in auctions, and the lowest offers win a guaranteed price for 15 years. The report says contracts should last 20 years instead. It also says payments should rise fully with inflation.

These changes could cut the cost of power from new onshore wind farms by about 11 per cent. If they had been used in the last auction, the price could have fallen from €97 to €69 for each megawatt hour.
Noel Cunniffe, the head of Wind Energy Ireland, said some changes could be ready for next year's auction. He said more wind farms are being built now than at any time in the last ten years.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭人付的電價是歐盟最高的。
一般家庭現在一年要付超過1,700歐元，比歐盟平均高出約50%。
一份新報告說，對一項綠能方案做些簡單的改變，可以幫助降低電費。
這份報告由顧問公司巴林加為代表風力產業的團體「愛爾蘭風能協會」撰寫。
報告在週一發表。
政府透過「再生電力支持方案」（RESS）來支持新的風場。
企業在競標中互相競爭，出價最低者可獲得15年的保證價格。
報告說合約應該改為20年。
報告也說補助金額應該完全隨通膨調升。
這些改變可讓新陸上風場的電力成本降低約11%。
如果上一次競標就採用這些做法，每百萬瓦時的價格可能會從97歐元降到69歐元。
愛爾蘭風能協會負責人諾爾・昆尼夫說，有些改變可以在明年的競標前準備好。
他說現在興建中的風場比過去十年任何時候都多。

paragraphs: Simple changes to the State's main green energy support scheme could lower electricity bills for homes and businesses by reducing the cost of wind power, according to a new industry report.

The study, carried out by consultants Baringa for Wind Energy Ireland, comes as Irish consumers pay the highest electricity prices in the EU. Typical household bills now exceed €1,700 a year, roughly 50 per cent above the European average.

Under the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme, developers bid in auctions and the lowest bids secure a guaranteed price for 15 years. Baringa recommends extending contracts for onshore wind to 20 years and fully linking payments to inflation, rather than the current 30 per cent indexation. Together, the reforms could reduce developers' costs by 23 per cent and cut the price of power from new onshore wind farms by around 11 per cent.
Had the changes applied at the most recent auction, the agreed price could have dropped from €97 to €69 per megawatt hour, the report says.

Wind Energy Ireland chief executive Noel Cunniffe said several measures could be introduced in time for next year's auction, noting that more onshore wind farms are under construction than at any point in the past decade.
sentZh: 根據一份新的產業報告，簡單調整國家主要的綠能補助方案，就能藉由降低風電成本，減少家庭和企業的電費。
這項由顧問公司巴林加為愛爾蘭風能協會進行的研究發表之際，愛爾蘭消費者正支付歐盟最高的電價。
一般家庭的電費帳單現在每年超過1,700歐元，比歐洲平均高出約50%。
在「再生電力支持方案」下，開發商參與競標，出價最低者可取得15年的保證價格。
巴林加建議將陸上風電合約延長至20年，並將補助完全與通膨連動，而非目前的30%指數化。
綜合起來，這些改革可使開發商成本降低23%，並使新陸上風場的電價下降約11%。
報告指出，如果上一次競標就適用這些改變，議定價格可能會從每百萬瓦時97歐元降到69歐元。
愛爾蘭風能協會執行長諾爾・昆尼夫說，數項措施可在明年競標前及時推出，並指出目前興建中的陸上風場數量是過去十年來最多的。

paragraphs: Modest, readily implemented tweaks to the State's flagship renewable energy subsidy could rein in electricity bills for households and businesses alike by curbing the cost of wind generation, an industry-commissioned report contends.

The analysis, undertaken by consultants Baringa on behalf of Wind Energy Ireland, lands at a time when Irish consumers are saddled with the steepest power prices in the EU, with typical household bills now topping €1,700 a year, some 50 per cent above the bloc's average.

Under the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme, developers compete in auctions in which the cheapest bids are awarded a guaranteed price for 15 years. Baringa advocates lengthening onshore contracts to 20 years and fully indexing payments to inflation, in place of the current 30 per cent. Taken together, these reforms could slash developers' costs by 23 per cent and trim the price of electricity from new onshore farms by roughly 11 per cent.
Had they been in force at the latest auction, the clearing price might have tumbled from €97 to €69 per megawatt hour.

Noel Cunniffe, the group's chief executive, maintained that several measures could be in place for next year's round, pointing out that more onshore wind farms are under construction than at any juncture in the past decade.

The analysis, conducted by the consultancy Baringa on behalf of Wind Energy Ireland, was published at a time when Irish consumers face the highest electricity prices in the European Union. Typical household bills currently exceed €1,700 annually, approximately 50 per cent above the EU average.

Under the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme, developers participate in competitive auctions, and the lowest bids receive a guaranteed price for 15 years. The report proposes extending onshore contracts to 20 years and fully indexing payments to inflation, as opposed to the existing 30 per cent. Consequently, developers' costs could decline by 23 per cent, and the price of electricity from new onshore wind farms could fall by approximately 11 per cent.
Had these measures been applied in the most recent auction, the clearing price would hypothetically have decreased from €97 to €69 per megawatt hour.

Noel Cunniffe, chief executive of Wind Energy Ireland, asserted that several reforms could be implemented prior to next year's auction, observing that the number of onshore wind farms under construction is at its highest level in a decade.

paragraphs: Simple changes to the State's main green energy support scheme could lower electricity bills for homes and businesses by reducing the cost of wind power, according to a new industry report.

The study, carried out by consultants Baringa for Wind Energy Ireland, comes as Irish consumers pay the highest electricity prices in the EU. Typical household bills now exceed €1,700 a year, roughly 50 per cent above the European average.

Under the Renewable Electricity Support Scheme, developers bid in auctions and the lowest bids secure a guaranteed price for 15 years. Baringa recommends extending contracts for onshore wind to 20 years and fully linking payments to inflation, rather than the current 30 per cent indexation. Together, the reforms could reduce developers' costs by 23 per cent and cut the price of power from new onshore wind farms by around 11 per cent.
Had the changes applied at the most recent auction, the agreed price could have dropped from €97 to €69 per megawatt hour, the report says.

Wind Energy Ireland chief executive Noel Cunniffe said several measures could be introduced in time for next year's auction, noting that more onshore wind farms are under construction than at any point in the past decade.
